name: penecho
description: Think with AI beyond the chat box. A shared canvas for handwriting, equations, diagrams, and spatial reasoning.
readmeHtml:
Not another AI agent. A better way to work with yours.

Draw what you mean, follow every job as a line, and let one agent check another's work.
Works with the agents you already use. Open source, free on your computer, no account needed.

Website  ·  Download  ·  Try in browser  ·  Agent leaderboard  ·  Discord  ·  Buy me a coffee

English · 简体中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Русский · Español · Português · Français · Deutsch

Install
Desktop app Download for macOS or Windows from penecho.ai.
npm npm install -g penecho, then penecho (Node.js 22.19 or newer).
Browser Open penecho.ai. Nothing to install.

Choose an access code, open a project folder, and add your agents in Settings → Agents. Use the agent plans you already pay for, your own API key, or PenEcho models.

New in 1.5.0: Lines, one-click review, the Orchestrator with real ratings, token savings with proof, and live Canvas sharing. See the changelog.

Run from source

You need Git and Node.js 22.19 or newer. The built pages are part of the repository, so there is no build step.

git clone https://github.com/penecho/penecho.git
cd penecho
npm install
npm start        # PenEcho opens at http://localhost:3888

For the desktop app from source, run npm run desktop:deps once, then npm run desktop. npm run check runs every check and test.

See it in 3 minutes

One real job from start to finish: one agent builds, another reviews, the fixes go back, and you make the last call.

▶ Watch the full film

Send a job straight to one agent, or hand it to the Orchestrator, which splits it and picks an agent for each part. Every agent works in your folder and keeps the same plain Markdown record.

What you get

Agents work together on one job
One agent builds, another reviews in one click, and Send fixes hands findings back on the same Line. 		Token savings, with proof
Continues or starts fresh, whichever costs less, and shows what every job saved.
An Orchestrator that learns
Splits big jobs, picks agents by their real record, and rates every result so picks improve over time. 		Every agent, synced
Sessions from Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, OpenCode and more sync in. Continue any of them with any agent.
Hundreds of jobs on one screen
Ask, Working, Needs you, To review, Done. See at a glance what waits for you. 		Draw what you mean
Circle a screenshot, sketch a prototype, make diagrams and slides. Agents see your marks with your words.
Plain Markdown you own
Every Line is a Markdown file in your folder, with one MEMORY.md for the project. Read it anywhere. 		Share with one link
Share a project or a Canvas with a link. Teammates open it in a browser to review and draw notes.

Works with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Antigravity, Kimi, Pi, DeepSeek Harness, omp, and PenEcho's built-in runner.

Canvas AI

Write, sketch, or circle something, and the answer lands right where you drew.

Sketch and ask — handwriting, equations, drawings, and mazes.

Kimi Open Source Friends

PenEcho is one of the Kimi Open Source Friends. Kimi Code runs in PenEcho like any other agent: add it in Settings → Agents, or get Kimi Code.

More

  • Community: Website · Leaderboard · Discord · Discussions · Issues · Contributing
  • Support: if PenEcho saved you an afternoon, buy us a coffee or sponsor on GitHub. A star or a good bug report helps just as much.
  • Docs: Architecture · Project Lines · MCP setup · Changelog
  • License: AGPL-3.0-only, with a commercial license available. See the trademark policy and CLA. Diagram renderers adapt code from Archify by tt-a1i (MIT); see NOTICE.

releases.name: PenEcho v1.5.0
releases.body:
## What's New

PenEcho 1.5.0 brings **PenEcho Lines**: run your projects with the AI agents already on your computer, and see every request, result and review on one page.

### Lines
- **Projects in a folder:** each project is a folder of plain Markdown files: your requests, the agents' results, notes and files. Nothing is locked inside the app.
- **One page per project:** requests, results, reviews, Canvases, files and merges sit together, drawn as lines you can follow.
- **Your own agents:** Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, omp, dsh, Kimi, Antigravity and PenEcho's own runner. Install, sign in and update them from Settings.

### Orchestrator and PenEcho Auto
- An agent can split a job and hand each part to the agent that does it best for its cost.
- Results get a review and a rating, and model prices are shown, so you can see what each part cost.

### Canvas
- **Collaborate:** one click makes a link anyone can draw on with you, live, with no account. A link lasts 7 days after its last change unless you sign in and save it.
- **Share and PDF:** view-only links update live as you work, and any Canvas downloads as a PDF.

releases.name: PenEcho v1.3.5
releases.body:
PenEcho v1.3.5 brings together the key improvements from 1.3.0–1.3.5, making the Canvas a more capable workspace for you and your AI agents.

## Highlights

- **Bring your own AI agent with MCP.** Connect Codex, Claude Code, Kimi, Cursor, or other compatible clients through Local MCP or Cloud MCP. Agents can read enabled Canvases, create and edit content, work with interactive Widgets, and respond to handwritten feedback.

- **Concurrent AI collaboration.** Canvas AI, PenEcho Agent, and MCP-connected agents can work on the same Canvas simultaneously. Agent workflows also gain improved file and document handling, conversation recovery, progress reporting, and thinking controls for supported models.

- **Professional diagrams.** Create architecture, sequence, and workflow diagrams with automatic layout and connection routing. Refine them through feedback or source edits, then export SVG or PNG. Rendering runs locally in the browser.

releases.name: PenEcho v1.3.3
releases.body:
## Professional Diagrams on the Canvas

PenEcho v1.3.3 introduces architecture diagrams, sequence diagrams, and workflows—with automatic layout, interactive details, and SVG/PNG export.

Create diagrams with PenEcho Agent or an MCP-connected AI agent, then refine them through feedback or source edits. Diagram layout and rendering run locally in your browser.

### Architecture Diagrams
Visualize services, dependencies, and nested system boundaries. Automatic layout and connection routing help keep complex systems readable.

### Sequence Diagrams
Describe interactions between participants with ordered messages, replies, self-calls, and activations. Model conditional, loop, and parallel scenarios.

### Workflows
Map processes with steps, decisions, labeled branches, loops, and parallel paths, including fork and join points.

## Improvements

- **Canvas Library:** Browse larger collections with pagination, search, project filters, and sorting. Previews load as cards become visible.

releases.name: PenEcho v1.3.2 — Canvas, MCP, and desktop improvements
releases.body:
## What's Changed

- Improved Canvas reliability and document handling.
- Improved MCP connection stability, session recovery, and PenEcho Agent responses.
- Refined desktop updates and Windows first-run behavior.
- Improved metadata routing and linked-device handling.
- Refreshed application icons, installer branding, and README visuals.


**Full Changelog**: [v1.3.1...v1.3.2](https://github.com/penecho/penecho/compare/v1.3.1...v1.3.2)

aiSummary.oneLiner: An AI-powered tool that renders answers as interactive diagrams and working widgets.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: PenEcho is a visual AI assistant that processes questions, sketches, or notes and returns interactive diagrams, documents, and working widgets. It integrates built-in AI capabilities and supports external MCP clients like Codex and Claude Code. Instead of just providing text responses, the tool visually demonstrates the answers directly beside the user's workspace. This interactive approach helps developers and designers quickly prototype ideas and visualize complex concepts.
keyFeatures: Visual responses: Renders answers as interactive diagrams and working widgets rather than just text.
Multimodal input: Accepts natural language questions, hand-drawn sketches, and structured notes.
MCP client support: Integrates seamlessly with external AI models via the Model Context Protocol.
Cross-platform availability: Offers native applications for macOS, Windows, and Linux environments.
Local installation: Provides an npm package for easy integration into existing JavaScript projects.

useCases.description: Convert hand-drawn sketches into working interactive widgets instantly using visual AI generation.

useCases.title: Visualizing complex architectures
useCases.description: Generate clear diagrams from text descriptions to explain system designs to engineering teams.

useCases.title: Augmenting coding agents
useCases.description: Connect external MCP clients like Claude Code to render their outputs visually.

useCases.title: Interactive learning
useCases.description: Ask technical questions and receive visual, executable examples alongside explanatory text.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Developers, designers, and systems architects who prefer visual learning and rapid prototyping. Requires basic knowledge of Node.js for npm installation.
